who is fighting for his right to decide his death he is speaking for himself and not other quadriplegics though his pioneering work depending on ones perspective may prove beneficial or damaging to quadriplegics down the road his primary objective is a personal one but one thing this movie does my opinion anyway is that it forces us the viewer to ask ourselves the referring questions my friend so succinct put forthafter my first viewing of the sea inside i walked home in a conflict blur i struggled to reconcile with this exasperating notion why would ran want to die given the love care and sacrifices so unconditionally showered on ran by the people surrounding him why would he doggedly cling on to his harmful decision then on my second viewing a shared thought between ran and the lawyer lady entered my consciousness it threw up a telling observation total dependency comes at the expense of intimacy most human beings grave for such an intimacy of course how much we value such needs depends largely on the individualas a person with a familiarbased sensibility i empathised strongly with the caregivers in this movie why cannot easier consider the sacrifice and the love from his family and friends is he blind to it all i would think not the miracle of the sea inside therefore is its insightful deduction of a very humanistic tug of war when we are faced with the guardianship of a sane but incapacitated loved one whom has expressed a calm conscious and rational intent to die what then is the right thing to do is daring for and keeping this loved one alive against his or her will a pious gesture does it show up the worth of our love or does it merely soothe our selfish fears of irreplaceable loss with so much understanding accorded to caregivers would not their invalid charges by submitting themselves to the total dependency of others for survival also be an overlooked act of sacrifice rhetoric or not how much is dignity worth to an individual is living or thing that the nature of sacrifice is never onesided in this tug of war we should endeavour not to win arguments but to intently observe and hopefully determine who is the stronger party to make that sacrificethe sea inside is a covering film it opened my eyes to things i do not anna see and for that i am grateful

saturday afternoon is one of harry londons bestknown short subjects and with good reason it is one of his funniest and best films the plot  such as it is  is an old staple a henpecked husband speaks away for a night out with a his pal and a couple of other girls it is a solid and wellused comedy plot but the difference here is harry london himself his slow ineffectual befuddled innocent character has somehow floundered his way into a marriage with a woman who feels that he of all people must be ruled with an iron fist and he is only thrust into cheating on her because he cannot say no to the exhortations of the clumsy vernon went and the cut eyelashesfluttering of the girl it is a very adult problem to be thrust onto such a helpless childlike character harry does not want to cheat but he cannot do anything about it in a wonderful bit of comic business he cannot bring himself to blow the new girlfriend kiss goodby he shyly pushes the kiss at her understand and ashamed wiped off his hand as if to chaste it the film is a threefeel comedy ten minutes longer than the tworevelers harry london had previously been starring in for mack bennett with no more plot perhaps it was even designed to be a tworeeled this works beautifully since it gives him as much time as he needs to inject the slow reactions and bewildered glimpses and halfactions where so much of his comedy lives he is at his best here and the show is really harry londons curious magic and ability to spin comedy out of almost nothing his little half smiles his look while handling the money he has hidden under the rug childlike attempts to enter the fight at the end i think his comedy makes us recognize something fundamentally innocent and confused in ourselves that makes us feel like the whole world is too much for us yet at the same time by allowing us to understand what harry does not such as the fact that the women he goodheartily brings to his friend to cheer him after he thinks the date has been blown are in fact shores he forces his to realize with a little bit of sadness that we are not that innocent anymore his comedy is just as capable of making us audibly say www as it is making us laugh often at once here harry wants to refuse to cheat on his wife he wants to tell his wife whose boss and take some power back in his relationship he wants to fight back against the two violent men at the end of the film but he just cannot affect his surroundings that much and sometimes we all feel like that the film is perfectly directed by frequent london director harry edwards it moves at a quick pace and never stalls while at the same time making time for and presenting to best effect harry londons still reactive comedy vernon went a frequent foil to london plays one of the roles here where he becomes almost a comedy partner in his very effective paring with harry the gas space out in a way that gives maximum effect too and harry gets his own version of a lloyd or reason style stung at the end here the comedy is not in harrys big reactions to the danger of sitting perched between two moving cars but in his slowness to take it in this is a hilarious film and a perfect example of the comedy of one of the most unique an talented humorist that i know ever to have existed

i saw this film at the 2004 toronto international film festival since i work in the wine business i had been quite eager to see this documentary and i was not disappointed reportedly drawn from over 500 hours of forage the good news is that nossiter will be releasing not only a theatrical cut but a tenpart ten hour series of the film on did by next christmas thinkfilm is distributing it the bad news is that it is still a bit of an unwieldy beast when it was shown in lannes it was close to three hours long for toronto he is cut about half an hour but it still blocked in at 135 minutes now for me that is fine i love wine and i love hearing about the controversies raging in my business but not everyone wants that muchnossiter fits around the globe from brazil to france to california to italy to argentina talking to wine makers and or people and consultant and critics about the state of the wine world the theme that emerges is that globalization and the undue influence of wine critic robert parker are forcing a kind of sameness on wine small local producers are either being bought up by larger conglomerates american as well as local or are being pressure by market forces to change their wines to suit the palate of mr parker who dictates taste to most of the american and world marketsit is a complicated subject and i can understand why nossiter wants to let his subjects talk there is robert monday patriarch of the papa wine industry and his sons tim and michael whose efforts to buy land in languedoc faced opposition from local vignerons and government officials there is aim hulbert founder and wine maker of drums vassar iconoclastic opponent of mondays plans and crusades for wines that express local terror there is robert parker himself expressing some discomfort with his influence while refusing to stop writing about the wines that he favours there is flying wine maker michel holland consultant for dozens of nineties all over the world advising them how to make parker friendly wines there are many many more fascinating personalities in this documentaryif you are a wine lover you will want to seek out the tenpart series as well as the theatrical version of this film but even if you are not into wine the film is an interesting look at how the forces of globalization are changing many of the worlds oldest and most established traditions the effects on local cultures and economies cannot be ignored810
